## Radial velocity mean correction (`SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE`) {#sec-ch12-mass-covariance}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Default: **off**. Enable with `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE=1`. The well-balanced x1 path converts density-weighted radial velocity to a
plain mean before reconstruction. Nonzero radial gravity requires at least three owned x1 cells at setup.
There is an existing setup-guard test, but no identified numerical accuracy oracle for this switch.
:::

### Derivation

On a Cartesian cell of width $h$ in metres, integrate two linear fields about its midpoint:
$h^{-1}\int_{-h/2}^{h/2}x_1\,\mathrm{d}x_1=0$ and
$h^{-1}\int_{-h/2}^{h/2}x_1^2\,\mathrm{d}x_1=h^2/12$.
Consequently the density-weighted velocity exceeds the plain velocity mean by
$(h^2/12)\partial_1\rho\partial_1v_1/\rho$. The code subtracts that leading term:

$$
\frac1h\int_{x_{1,i-1/2}}^{x_{1,i+1/2}}v_1\,\mathrm{d}x_1
\simeq\frac{\langle\rho v_1\rangle_{V_i}}{\langle\rho\rangle_{V_i}}
-\frac{h^2}{12\rho_i}\partial_1\rho_i\partial_1v_{1,i}.
$$ {#eq-ch12-mass-covariance-mean}

The left side is integration with the uniform radial measure, not a newly stored field.
`rho_1` and `w1` implement @eq-ch12-mass-covariance-mean ([`hydro_forward.cpp:314-352`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L314-L352)).
The integral identity is exact for linear fields; substituting finite differences and nonlinear profiles introduces
truncation. `configuration_check.py` verifies the identity with rational polynomial integration.
This is re-derived from the implementation; no standalone derivation note was identified.

### Numerical method

The radial gravity/non-shallow-water path computes centered density and velocity differences. At reflecting walls,
a three-owned-cell one-sided density slope replaces the slope through the reflected ghost. The corrected velocity
has odd wall ghosts, is reconstructed with the density/pressure perturbations, and is then restored in the input
array. The correction is part of each explicit hydro call; it is not a new implicit matrix term.
